headline: Maine menhaden fishery set to close Sunday as quota nears completion
dek: The state says harvesters have landed 98.7% of Maine's available menhaden quota, extending a season shaped by a 20% coastwide cut and transfers from other states.
body: Maine's commercial Atlantic menhaden season is scheduled to close Sunday night after state regulators said harvesters had landed 98.7% of the available quota, a deadline that will affect the bait supply used by lobster and other coastal fisheries.

The Maine Department of Marine Resources said in a September 28 notice that it expected the remaining quota to be taken after additional fishing on September 28 and October 1. The department set the closure for 11:59 p.m. Sunday, October 4, and told harvesters to complete their final reports. The notice applies to all menhaden harvesters, even though the department's general 2026 season framework had listed May 1 through November 30 as the season window. The current closure notice is at https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MEDMR/bulletins/42cdf35.

The compressed ending reflects a difficult quota year. The Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission reduced the coastwide total allowable catch for 2026 to 186,840 metric tons, a 20% decrease from the prior level. Maine's Department of Marine Resources said the reduction was intended to lower fishing mortality while protecting predators such as striped bass. Maine's preliminary state quota was set at 19,599,137 pounds, with another 4,119,117 pounds reserved for its Episodic Event Set-Aside program. The agency's management page is https://www.maine.gov/dmr/fisheries/commercial/fisheries-by-species/menhaden-atlantic/menhaden-management.

Maine officials also said transfers from partner states helped keep the directed fishery open into October. The department said it received twice as much transferred quota as in the previous effort, despite the coastwide reduction. That choice allowed fishermen to keep using purse seines rather than shifting in mid-September to the small-scale provision, which carries different gear and quota rules. The state described the decision as a way to preserve additional harvest opportunity while staying within the available allocation.

The stakes extend beyond the boats that catch menhaden. The Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission describes menhaden as a forage species for striped bass, bluefish and weakfish, and says commercial bait landings are used mostly in lobster, crab and hook-and-line fisheries. The commission's species overview says the 2026 quota has a zero-percent modeled chance of overfishing under its current assessment, while the stock is not classified as overfished. Those findings do not remove the economic effect of a smaller quota on bait users. SeafoodSource reported that Maine lobster groups viewed the 20% cut as less severe than proposals for reductions of more than 50%, while still warning that any cut could affect the small-boat fleet: https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/supply-trade/asmfc-cuts-atlantic-menhaden-quota-by-20-percent-in-2026.

The next debate is already underway. The commission has scheduled a virtual public hearing for 6 p.m. Thursday, October 1, on Draft Addendum II to the interstate menhaden plan. The proposal considers reducing the Chesapeake Bay reduction-fishery cap by as much as 50% and distributing that cap more evenly over the fishing season. The commission says the options are intended to address concentrated fishing effort and possible ecological effects in the bay. Public comments are due by 11:59 p.m. October 9. Hearing and comment details are available at https://asmfc.org/events/general-public-hearing-on-atlantic-menhaden-draft-addendum-ii/.

For Maine harvesters, the immediate question is operational: how much quota remains after the final scheduled fishing day and how will the closure affect bait inventories heading into the fall lobster season. The Department of Marine Resources has not announced an extension beyond October 4 in its current notice. Longer-term decisions will come through the interstate process, with the commission expected to discuss menhaden quotas for 2027 and 2028 during its October 2026 annual meeting.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Maine menhaden fishery to close October 4 after quota nears completion
seoDescription: Maine's menhaden season is set to close October 4 after 98.7% of the quota was landed, with lobster bait and future regional rules in focus.
